Alyssa — thanks for the thoughtful list. Short answers up front, then specifics below so your procurement team has language to work with.

Summary bullets
- We support both monthly reserved commits (month-to-month) and annual prepay (12-month commitment) for Dedicated GPU pools. Annual prepay gets a stepped discount (typically 10–18% depending on commit size).
- True-ups: if you prepay annually and exceed committed throughput, we bill overage on a monthly basis at the agreed overage rate with pro-rating for partial months. We also offer a mid-year top-up that converts additional capacity into discounted committed spend for the remainder of the term.
- Monthly reserved commits provide capacity guarantees for the month but are subject to availability for bursts; we offer optional burst credits you can purchase ahead of need.
- Standard commercial PO workflow with Net30 is supported; we can accept ACH and wire. I attached a sample invoice template and a revised proposal (PDF).

Details (copyable language for Procurement)
1) Pricing and commit types
   - Monthly Reserved: invoiced at the start of each month for the reserved GPU pool. No long-term discount. Throughput guarantee applies to baseline reserved capacity; burst capacity is available against spare pools and billed separately.
   - Annual Prepay (12-month): invoiced as an upfront prepayment or as 4 quarterly invoices (as requested by finance); eligible for discount tiers based on committed spend. Prepay locks price and capacity for the term.

2) True-ups and overages
   - If usage <= committed throughput: no additional charges.
   - If usage > committed throughput: overage billed monthly at agreed overage rates. For annual prepay customers, overage rates are a negotiated percentage of list (typically 1.2x list overage or can be added to next top-up).
   - Mid-term Top-up: customer can convert overage into additional committed capacity with retroactive credit for the month of conversion (pro-rated). Example: committed 16 GPUs, spike pushes to 20 GPUs for 3 months; you can opt to add 4 GPUs to committed for the remaining 9 months; invoicing will pro-rate the new commit and apply credit for months already paid.

3) Invoicing, PO, payment terms
   - We provide an invoice template with line items: Reserved capacity (GPU-hours/machine-type), Support (standard/premium), Burst credits (if purchased), Taxes.
   - PO number required on invoice for procurement matching. Net30 standard; Net45 available for enterprise with reference to legal agreements. ACH and wire accepted.

4) SLA and remedies
   - Throughput guarantees are contractual for reserved capacity; SLA credits apply for downtime or sustained degradation beyond thresholds. Bursts are best-effort and not SLA-backed.
